F01.P1.notes: Immutable const local binding, no reassignment, returned as function result.

F01.P2.fragment_summary: let counter: bigint = 0n; const LIMIT: bigint = 100n;
F01.P2.notes: bigint chosen over number because number cannot represent the full 64-bit signed range (safe-integer limit 2^53-1); bigint is a documented distinct TS/JS numeric type meeting the range requirement. let vs const gives the required mutable/immutable distinction.

F02.P1.fragment_summary: let v: number; if (cond) { v = 5; } else { v = 9; } return v;
F02.P1.notes: TypeScript definite-assignment control-flow analysis accepts this under --strict because both branches assign v before use.

F02.P2.fragment_summary: const buf = new Uint8Array(16); buf[0] = 1; const x = buf[0]; return x;
F02.P2.notes: JS/TS TypedArray storage is always zero-initialized per ECMA-262; no documented mechanism yields genuinely uninitialized bulk storage. R9-named substitution (default-initialized buffer) used per canonical_task's own exception, drops the 'uninitialized' sub-requirement -> PARTIAL under P-a.

F03.P2.notes: In-place element mutation through existing array binding.

F04.P1.citation: ECMA-262 primitive value semantics: numbers are passed and bound by value; JS/TS has no address-of, pointer, ref, or inout mechanism giving two names write access to one scalar's storage in the same scope.
F04.P1.notes: Wrapping the scalar in an object would change the value/storage kind being denoted and is not a named R9 substitution for this probe; canonical_task instructs NONE with reason when unavailable.

F04.P2.fragment_summary: const window: ReadonlyArray<number> = xs; return window[0];
F04.P2.notes: TypeScript ReadonlyArray/readonly modifier is a documented, standard, non-copying compile-time view over an existing array; --strict is the frozen recipe posture recognizing this type-level guarantee (typescript_strict_clause).

F04.P3.fragment_summary: class Obj{id:number;constructor(id:number){this.id=id;}} const first=new Obj(5); const arr=[first]; const second=arr[0]; const same = first === second; return same;
F04.P3.notes: JS/TS `===` on non-primitive operands is reference-identity comparison per ECMA-262, distinct from structural/value equality.

F05.P1.notes: Ordinary bare call site; no sigil/marker exists in JS/TS call syntax regardless of aliasing outcome.

F05.P2.citation: No JS/TS mechanism (ref/inout/pointer/address-of) lets a callee write a caller's scalar local variable; canonical_task explicitly forbids a mutable-object-wrapper substitute from counting as FULL.
F05.P2.notes: Consistent with F04.P1: JS/TS scalars are always passed by value.

F05.P3.fragment_summary: const neg = (a: number): number => k - a; const ys = xs.map(neg); return ys[0];
F05.P3.notes: Arrow function captures enclosing k by closure; Array.prototype.map applies neg by name.

F06.P1.fragment_summary: function mid(xs: number[]): number { return xs[1]; } const y = mid(xs); return y;
F06.P1.notes: Element type is primitive number; return is a value copy by language rule.

F06.P2.fragment_summary: function divmod2(a:number,b:number):[number,number]{return [Math.trunc(a/b), a % b];} const [q,r]=divmod2(a,b); return q+r;
F06.P2.notes: Tuple type + array destructuring is the standard TS multi-result idiom.

F07.P1.notes: Ordinary operator precedence, no redundant parens.

F07.P2.fragment_summary: const q = Math.trunc(a / b); const m = a % b; const d = a / b;
F07.P2.notes: number is already IEEE-754 double so d needs no conversion; Math.trunc gives truncating integer division; % gives remainder with sign of dividend.

F08.P1.notes: Rung (ii) wrapping: bitwise `|0` invokes ECMA-262 ToInt32, a documented, deterministic 32-bit wraparound conversion; rung (i) checked-optional op does not exist in JS/TS.

F08.P2.notes: Rung (ii) explicit local guard on b===0, since rung (i) checked-division-to-optional does not exist and the plain operator does not trap.

F09.P1.notes: JS strings are primitive values; === compares contents, not object identity, per ECMA-262 Strict Equality Comparison.

F09.P2.fragment_summary: xs.sort((a,b) => b - a); const lt = a < b;
F09.P2.notes: Array.prototype.sort mutates in place; explicit descending comparator supplied by value.

F10.P1.notes: Rung (ii): BigInt.asIntN(32,_) is a documented standard wrapping narrowing of a 64-bit-capable bigint to signed 32-bit range; no checked-optional rung (i) exists.

F10.P2.notes: TS unifies int/float under `number` (IEEE-754 double); no conversion is written or performed because none is required by the language.

F11.P1.notes: Ordinary array indexing never traps; out-of-range yields `undefined` at runtime (a documented ECMA-262 behavior), which is the primary measured form.

F11.P2.notes: Array.prototype.slice is the standard sub-range operation; it copies elements (documented), so part is independent storage.

F12.P1.fragment_summary: let o: number | undefined = undefined; const n: number = o ?? 0; return n;
F12.P1.notes: Union-with-undefined is TS's standard optionality encoding; `??` is the standard nullish-coalescing fallback form.

F12.P2.fragment_summary: function h(x:number):number{return x+1;} let p: number|undefined; if (o !== undefined) { p = h(o); } else { p = undefined; } const result = p !== undefined ? p : 0;
F12.P2.notes: JS/TS standard library has no Option/Maybe map/chain operation over a T|undefined union; canonical_task names this probe's substitution explicitly (R9 list). Explicit conditional used, dropping the 'without explicit if' requirement -> PARTIAL under P-a.

F13.P1.fragment_summary: function parseTwice(s:string):number { const n=Number(s); if (Number.isNaN(n)) throw new Error('bad'); return n*2; }
F13.P1.notes: Explicit throw on the standard conversion's failure signal (NaN), propagated unhandled to the caller; idiomatic JS/TS failure-signaling pattern given the absence of a checked parse.

F13.P2.fragment_summary: const parsed = Number(s); const n = Number.isNaN(parsed) ? 0 : parsed; return n;
F13.P2.notes: If-error form is the language's normal local-handling idiom given Number()'s NaN failure signal.

F14.P1.fragment_summary: type Shape = {kind:'circle', r:number} | {kind:'rect', w:number, h:number}; const s: Shape = {kind:'circle', r:2.0};
F14.P1.notes: Discriminated union type alias is closed: no external code can add a member to this specific union declaration.

F14.P2.fragment_summary: switch(s.kind){case 'circle': return Math.PI*s.r*s.r; case 'rect': return s.w*s.h;}
F14.P2.notes: TS control-flow narrowing over a discriminated union reduces the residual type to `never` only when all members are covered; an omitted case is a genuine compile error ('not all code paths return a value'), i.e. documented exhaustiveness checking.

F14.P3.fragment_summary: shapes.ts: interface Shape{area():number;} class Circle implements Shape{...} class Rect implements Shape{...}; app.ts: class Tri implements Shape{...}; const s: Shape = new Tri(...); return s.area();
F14.P3.notes: Interface+class extensibility across ES module files is TS's standard open-polymorphism mechanism; multi-unit recipe unchanged per toolchain_binding.multi_unit_recipes (TS already follows module imports).

F15.P1.fragment_summary: function head<T>(xs:T[]):T { return xs[0]; } const a = head([4,5,6]); const b = head(['p','q']); return String(a)+b;
F15.P1.notes: Single generic function reused at two instantiations with a statically recoverable T->T result relationship.

F15.P2.fragment_summary: function max_of<T extends number>(a:T,b:T):T { return a > b ? a : b; } const m = max_of(3,5); return m;
F15.P2.notes: TS/JS ships no standard ordering abstraction (no Comparable/Ord trait) usable as a declaration-site generic bound; substituted a concrete `extends number` bound per the canonical_task's own named exception for this probe (R9 list) -> PARTIAL under P-a.

F15.P3.fragment_summary: interface Named{tag():string;} class A implements Named{tag(){return 'a';}} class B implements Named{tag(){return 'b';}} const items: Named[]=[new A(), new B()]; return items[0].tag();
F15.P3.notes: Heterogeneous array typed by an abstract interface with virtual-method dispatch at runtime.

F16.P1.fragment_summary: const xs: number[] = [1,2,3]; const total = xs.reduce((a,b)=>a+b, 0); return total;
F16.P1.notes: Array.prototype.reduce is the standard sum/fold operation.

F16.P2.fragment_summary: const mp = new Map<string,number>([['a',1]]); let total=0; for (const [,v] of mp) total+=v; const miss = mp.get('b') ?? 0; return total+miss;
F16.P2.notes: ECMA-262 Map guarantees insertion-order iteration (documented); Map.prototype.get returns undefined on miss, handled via `??`.

F17.P1.fragment_summary: function readAll():number{ const fd=fs.openSync('data.txt','r'); try { const text=fs.readFileSync(fd,'utf8'); return Buffer.byteLength(text); } finally { fs.closeSync(fd); } }
F17.P1.notes: try/finally is JS/TS's normal deterministic scoped-cleanup idiom; the finally block executes on every exit path including the failure path.

F17.P2.fragment_summary: class Handle{id:number; constructor(id:number){this.id=id;} dispose(){released++;}} let released=0; { const h=new Handle(1); try{} finally{ h.dispose(); } } return released;
F17.P2.notes: JS/TS has no deterministic garbage-collector-driven end-of-lifetime hook (FinalizationRegistry is explicitly documented as non-deterministic and unsuitable for reliance); used the R9-named nearest standard construct (explicit dispose invoked by a scoped try/finally) -> PARTIAL under P-a.

F18.P1.notes: Global console facility requires no import declaration in Node; satisfies canonical_task's 'nothing if available without one' clause.

F18.P2.fragment_summary: util.ts: export function pub_add(a:number,b:number){return a+b+secret();} function secret(){return 1;}  main.ts: import {pub_add} from './util.js'; return pub_add(2,3);
F18.P2.notes: ES module export lists enforce the visibility boundary at the language level; non-exported bindings are inaccessible from other modules. Multi-unit recipe unchanged per toolchain_binding.

F19.P1.fragment_summary: async function main(){ const p1=(async()=>20)(); const p2=(async()=>22)(); const [a,b]=await Promise.all([p1,p2]); return a+b; }
F19.P1.notes: async/await + Promise.all is the standard built-in concurrency facility; single-threaded cooperative async explicitly counts per canonical_task.

F19.P2.fragment_summary: let counter=0; async function incr(){ for(let i=0;i<1000;i++) counter++; } async function main(){ await Promise.all([incr(), incr()]); return counter; }
F19.P2.notes: No await occurs inside either loop, so each async function body runs to completion without interleaving under ECMA-262's documented run-to-completion (Jobs) semantics; this is a normative language guarantee, not an empirical accident, so the result is deterministically 2000 on every run (verification: 20/20 consecutive runs observed at 2000).

F20.P1.citation: Node.js/TypeScript ship no built-in FFI mechanism callable without either a third-party package (e.g. node-ffi-napi) or a separately built native addon (node-gyp/N-API), both of which are outside the frozen tsc/node recipe and violate R7.
F20.P1.notes: No documented standard mechanism meets the baseline_condition.

F20.P2.citation: The frozen recipe (`tsc ...; node FILE.js`) produces JS source run by the Node VM, not a compiled artifact with a platform symbol table; there is no unmangled, nm-visible external symbol to produce.
F20.P2.nm_evidence: no compiled artifact under the frozen recipe
